evals.prompt: Make an App Store preview video for Sample Recipes. We already have the screenshots done with a locked style. Just make it, the app's the usual demo build.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads Apple's preview rules and proposes a storyboard (three to five beats in 15 to 30 seconds, each with one headline, the moment it shows, the camera and any emphasis; the poster frame at 5 s; the end card with an account and subscription disclosure), then stops for the user's agreement before recording or writing an edit, despite 'just make it'.
expectations: The agent proposes a storyboard as a table or ordered list of beats, each with a headline of about 2 to 5 words and the app moment it shows
The core value appears in the first beat
The agent says which frame is the poster frame (5 s by default) and what it shows
The end card includes a disclosure of an account requirement or subscription, or the agent asks the user for those facts
The agent proposes using the locked screenshot style for the look
The agent stops for the user's agreement before recording takes or running compose.py

evals.prompt: Here's our edit for the Sample Recipes iPhone preview (examples/sample-edit.json). The recipe card highlight is a bit off the card and the corners of the highlight don't line up. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent measures the card's rect and corner radius from the dumped frame's pixels at the spotlight's time (not the UI tree or a guess), sets rect to the card itself, r to the card's own radius and an even pad, renders a still at the spotlight's settled time with compose.py --frames N --stills, opens it at full size, and reports what it saw.
expectations: The agent measures the element from the dumped frames' pixels rather than guessing
The agent sets r to the element's own corner radius and uses pad for the margin, so the hole's corners are concentric
The agent renders a still at the spotlight's time with compose.py --frames and --stills
The agent opens the still and describes whether the margin is even on every side

evals.prompt: Can we zoom right into the calorie number on the Sample Recipes preview so people can read it, maybe 2x? And speed up the typing part so it's shorter.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that Apple advises against zooming and that the camera stops where the whole device fits, offering a spotlight on the element instead; and that typing should stay at a person's pace (record with rate 4 to 6, play it with step 1), offering to shorten the beat by cutting dead time with holds rather than speeding up the typing.
expectations: The agent does not set a camera scale that crops the device frame
The agent mentions Apple's guidance against zooming into the app or showing the app faster than it is
The agent offers a spotlight (or the push-in to the whole device) as the alternative
The agent offers to shorten the typing beat by cutting dead time with holds or a shorter take, not by stepping through the typing

evals.prompt: We need the preview for the iPhone Duo too. The open screen is really wide.
evals.expected_output: The agent says the Duo preview is the same 886x1920 size as other iPhones, and proposes one video carrying both postures: the cover display's take with a foldable-outer frame, then a slide to the open display as a second footage (foldable-inner, pan true) panned a pane at a time; it warns that the open display's recording may dump squeezed and to force its landscape shape with video.py frames --size.
expectations: The agent states the iPhone Duo preview size is 886x1920 (or 1920x886)
The agent proposes showing both the folded (cover) and open displays in one video
The agent uses a panned second footage for the open display rather than shrinking it to fit or cropping it
The agent mentions the squeezed rotated recording and video.py frames --size
